about: The verified examples (issue #187): the owner's SLT questions of 17 Nov, each with his definition and the exact semantic query that answers it. A plan names its window by a relative window of the semantic model's defaults block, read on the page's day; with no window said it is the year to date (the no_window default), and the alternates are the period to date, last week and the previous period. Every plan is validated against the semantic model when the file loads (examples.load), and tests/test_examples.py checks every example's rows against a hand-written SQL query over the record tables at two anchors, so no expected number is typed anywhere. reviewed_by is owner-pending until the owner checks the numbers; each example carries five rewordings, owner-pending, beside his own words, and the reading score asks each of the offline router (evals/run.py, /evals).

examples.question: What are the top three contributors to speed loss?
examples.definition: Feet lost against each grade's baseline, by contributor, top 3
examples.notes: The contributors are the owner's to rule (owner-pending, the defaults' speed_loss rule): each unplanned stop reason's minutes at the stopped setup's grade baseline, and each grade's speed gap (its paper runs' feet under the baseline while running, targets.json), ranked together in feet. Planned maintenance (schedule-driven) and a power outage (external) are left out of the stops.

examples.question: What are our best running grades?
examples.definition: Ranked by lineal ft/min (running), beside each grade's baseline, with the gap and the footage recoverable by closing it
examples.notes: The best of the two readings of 'best and worst running grades'. Beside each grade: its baseline, the footage recoverable (targets.json's speed gap: each of the grade's paper runs that ran under the baseline, the feet it would have made at the baseline less the feet it made, summed) and that gap in ft/min over all the grade's running minutes. A grade that ran faster than its baseline on average can still have runs under it, so its gap is never negative.
